title: State-Dependent Diffusion and Spectra of Strongly Driven Thermal Atoms
authors: Zheng Xiao, Zijie Liu, Suyang Wei, Anhong Dang, Tiantian Shi, Jingbiao Chen
abstract: We propose a state-dependent diffusion model for strongly driven thermal-atom spectra. Starting from the trajectory-dependent internal-state evolution of individual atoms, we derive a closed spatial equation for the local density-matrix field using a velocity-moment expansion. Measurements of an $^{85}$Rb atomic-filter transmission spectrum agree well with the model up to a maximum Gaussian peak intensity of $1.27\times10^{3}$ W/cm$^2$, approaching six orders of magnitude above the $^{85}$Rb D2-line saturation intensity. Counterintuitively, the model reveals an anomalous optical-pumping pathway in which intense light transfers atoms from nominally dark states into bright states. Hyperfine Paschen--Back splitting selectively enhances this anomalous pathway while suppressing conventional optical pumping, allowing the filter to maintain approximately 97$\%$ transmission at the highest intensity studied. This work provides a framework for controlling strongly driven atomic ensembles and designing saturation-resistant atomic optical devices.
summary: This research develops a state-dependent diffusion model to describe the optical response of thermal atomic ensembles under intense laser driving. By analyzing the internal-state dynamics, the authors predict an anomalous optical-pumping mechanism that resists saturation. This framework is crucial for designing robust, high-performance atomic optical devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses deriving experimentally accessible continuum fields from the microscopic, state-dependent internal-state dynamics of a thermal ensemble of strongly driven atoms.
main_result: The model reveals an anomalous optical-pumping pathway, enhanced by hyperfine Paschen-Back splitting, which allows the atomic filter to maintain high transmission ($\approx 97\%$) even at intensities far exceeding saturation levels.
method: The authors derive a closed spatial equation for the local density-matrix field using a velocity-moment expansion applied to the semiclassical phase-space master equation.
model_or_system: The system involves strongly driven thermal atoms (specifically $^{85}	ext{Rb}$) interacting with intense optical fields. The theoretical framework uses a density-matrix approach, evolving from a phase-space master equation to a diffusion-form master equation.
key_observables: Local density-matrix field ($ ar{\varrho}$), transmission spectra (Faraday anomalous-dispersion optical filter), and spatial population distributions.
important_parameters: High light intensities (up to $1.27	imes10^{3}$ W/cm$^2$), hyperfine Paschen–Back splitting strength, and the ratio of spontaneous emission to driving field strength.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on a velocity-moment expansion and assumes that collisions maintain a local Maxwell distribution, leading to a mode-dependent transport operator.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the reduction from the phase-space master equation to the local density-matrix field, show spatially resolved population dynamics under different magnetic fields, and display the FADOF transmission spectra at varying powers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the full phase-space kinetic equation, deriving the closed spatial equation for the local density-matrix field via moment expansion, analyzing the resulting transport dynamics, and finally validating the model against high-intensity experimental measurements of the atomic filter spectrum.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized framework for modeling open quantum systems in the presence of strong driving fields, moving beyond simple scalar diffusion approximations by incorporating mode-dependent transport dictated by internal atomic states.
